title: About hmt-apps
text:
Throughout the first quarter of the twenty-first century, the Homer Multitext project’s (HMT) work on Homeric manuscripts intentionally prioritized building openly licensed data sets in simple plain-text formats over developing apps. Major components of the archive include (among other things):

collections of digital images of Homeric manuscripts
cataloged data about manuscripts of the Iliad
editions of texts of the Iliad and scholia
indexes associating texts, manuscript pages, and images
other indexes including proper nouns and adjectives

This fundamental decision about how to distribute its work is epitomized in the publication of the HMT archive in a single plain-text file, that is always available in its most recent release on github, here.

title: About hmt-apps
text:
“Two-coffee apps”
This repository is a personal project inspired by the potential of coding agents like Claude. Working with the HMT project’s data releases constantly inspires new ideas for apps to explore the complex interrelationships in the HMT data. With an agentic assistant, it’s now remarkably straightforward to draft working versions of these ideas very quickly. I developed each of the apps linked here to a point where I was comfortable releasing it on github in less time than it took me to finish two cups of coffee. The initial investment in both time and coffee is small enough that if an idea doesn’t work out, I can throw it away without hesitation. This dramatically accelerated release cycle gives new meaning to Eric Raymond’s famous aphorism, “Release early, release often.” By reducing the effort to build an app, coding agents can be a boon to scholars with expertise in particular subject matter, rather than in software engineering.
All of the apps in this repository start by downloading the HMT project’s latest data release. Apps quickly developed by agents like Claude amplify the value of the data, and offer a powerful new justification for the HMT project’s decision to favor developing datasets over software.

title: Documentation for individual apps
text:
Citable connections across HMT data
Throughout the HMT archive, texts are related to physical artifacts documented by citable images. All apps for browsing texts, manuscript pages or images can be bookmarked by a URN for manuscript page (page), textual passage (text) or image (image).

title: Documentation for individual apps

Text formatting and navigation
All textual displays organize the display of passages by physical page, and support previous/next navigation.

title: Browse images
text: images.html: a light box of HMT image collections, with pannable, zoomable views of individual images.

title: Browse images
text: images.html: a light box of HMT image collections, with pannable, zoomable views of individual images.

title: Browse images
text:
User options and display
In light-table view:

Collection menu: choose an image collection.
Find: search caption of images.
Size slider: adjust width of the thumbnails.
Select an image to open it in single-image view.

In single-image view:

‹ › (or [ and ]): move to previous or next image of the collection.
Rights: shows/hide rights statement.
← Images (or Esc): return to light box view.
Navigation: drag to pan; scroll or pinch to zoom; +, − and Fit (or the +, - and 0 keys).

If the image server cannot be reached, the thumbnails show “no image”.

title: Browse images
text:
Optional URL parameters

image — an image URN. Collection-level URN opens in lightbox view, e.g. ?image=urn:cite2:hmt:vaimg.2017a:. Object-level URN opens in single image view, e.g. urn:cite2:hmt:vaimg.2017a:VA091RN_0092
page — a page URN, e.g. urn:cite2:hmt:msA.v1:12r: opens the reference image for that page.
text — a CTS URN. Opens the image the passage is indexed to.

If multiple parameters are given, image takes priority, then page, then text

title: Browse images
text:
Data sources
From the HMT release:

#!datamodels (image model urn:cite2:cite:datamodels.v1:imagemodel), #!citecollections and #!citedata: the image collections and their items (URN, caption, rights).
Only for the page and text parameters: the codex pages (#!datamodels codex model, #!citedata) and the DSE (#!citerelationset, urn:cite2:hmt:hmtdse.v1:all).
#!citelibrary: the release name in the status line.
The pictures are not in the release: they are fetched from the HMT IIIF image server, at an address worked out from each image URN. A picture’s pixel size is read from its IIIF info.json when it is opened.
The release (hmt-current.cex) is fetched when the page opens; if that fails, a saved copy can be dropped on the page or chosen with the file picker.

title: Where should I start?
text:
The HMT archive is large and complex. Rather than try to produce a comprehensive HMT app, I am experimenting with numerous small, focused apps. The list of currently running apps has grown to the point it might not be obvious how to get started. Here are some suggestions.

if you want to read editions of the Iliad and scholia, try iliad-scholia.html
if you want to browse manuscript fascimiles, try our most completely edited manuscript, the Venetus A.
if you want to browse the HMT project’s collection of manuscript images, try images.html

title: Simple text search
text:
User options and display

Type a Greek string (at least two letters; accents, breathings, capitals and punctuation do not matter). Press Search; typing also searches after a short pause.
Choose where to search: all texts, Iliad or scholia; and the text searched and shown: diplomatic or normalized.
Matching passages are listed under the word forms that contain the string, by version (60 at a time, with a “show more” button). Choosing one shows its manuscript page: the Iliad lines and scholia on it, every match marked, the scholia panels with a match unfolded.
Every manuscript page in the page view has ‹ Previous page and Next page › buttons: the page before or after in the codex, even one with no indexed text. The marks stay on the passages that match.

title: Simple text search
text:
Optional URL parameters
Unlike the browsing apps, this app still keeps its state in a # hash (no query-string parameters); the address follows the search, so bookmarks and Back and Forward work.

#q=<string>&s=<all|iliad|scholia>&t=<diplomatic|normalized>[&p=<passage>] — the string; where to search (s, default all); the text searched and shown (t, default diplomatic); and the passage chosen (p).

title: Simple text search
text:
Data sources

#!ctscatalog and #!ctsdata: the texts searched.
For the page view of a chosen passage: #!citerelationset (the DSE urn:cite2:hmt:hmtdse.v1:all and the commentary index urn:cite2:hmt:commentary.v1:all, found through #!datamodels), #!datamodels, #!citecollections and #!citedata (codex pages and their labels); #!citelibrary (release name in the status line).
The release (hmt-current.cex) is fetched when the page opens; if that fails, a saved copy can be dropped on the page or chosen with the file picker.

title: Iliad + scholia reader
text:
User options and display

Version of the Iliad: choose a manuscript.
Text: display diplomatic or normalized Iliad edition.
Passage: a line (1.5), a range (1.1-1.10) or a whole book (1)
Show: displays requested passage highlighted, along with all other text on the same manuscript page.
Scholia count: appears next to a line commented on by scholia. Click the button to show scholia refernces; selecting a scholion displays its text.
Unfold/fold all scholia unfolds or folds up all scholia on a page.
‹ Previous page and Next page ›: display a single preceding or following page.

title: Iliad + scholia reader
text:
Optional parameters

text — a CTS URN, shows all text indexed to that page, highlighting the requested passage. Example: ?text=urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0012.tlg001.msA:1.1-1.10.
page — a page URN. Shows text indexed to that page.
image — an image URN. Shows the text indexed to that image.

If multiple parameters are given, text takes priority, then page, then image.

title: Links across apps
text:
Links from text displays
In all text browsing and text searching apps, text displays are organized by manuscript page. Each page label is linked to a full display of the page in codices.html. Each passage reference (Iliad line, scholion identifier) is linked to codices.html with the region of interest for that specific passage highlighted.
